label: rem:hadron-q-self-correction-interpretation
title: Novelty of substrate self-deformation by linking density
html:
Remark (Topological back-reaction). The signed-crossing excess \binom{p}{2} - \binom{n}{2} acts as a topological self-deformation of the substrate field. Nuclear linking density \ell_{\mathrm{net}}/A^2 drives this. This provides a geometric mechanism for nuclear self-correction.

Effect on beta decay: the differential shift

In beta decay, A remains fixed while (p, n) shifts by (+1, -1). The daughter nucleus exhibits a different self-deformation from the parent. The change in effective q across the decay is

  \Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}}
  = 
  \delta q(p+1, n-1) - \delta q(p, n)
  = 
  \frac{A - 1}{A^2} \cdot \hbar_q^2.

This shift is strictly positive. The daughter acquires one more proton and thus more positive crossings, yielding a higher effective q; a higher q increases the crossing asymmetry, giving a larger Q-value (transition energy) than predicted by the background alone. The Sargent rule f(Q) \propto Q^5 applies, so the enlarged Q-value increases the decay rate and shortens the half-life.

The shift \Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}} is exactly the q-anomaly \delta_q of the transition energy: the daughter is evaluated at the shifted q + \Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}}, not the background q. This embodies q-deformed energy balance, overriding classical conservation.

Effect on the decay rate

The differential shift \Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}} modifies the effective substrate parameter at the converting nucleon. The decay rate depends on q with sensitivity \approx 48 (half-life regimes). A shift of \Delta q / q_0 \sim 0.1--0.4\% induces a measurable change in the decay rate.

For {}^{3}\mathrm{H} (A = 3), the shift \Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}} = (2/9) \times \hbar_q^2 \approx 0.00218 is the maximum correction. This categorical quantity derives directly from q, A, and the linking structure of the nuclear braid.

Universality

The self-deformation applies whenever q acts on a specific hadron configuration. This extends beyond half-lives: the beta-stability line (beta-stability) and the topological mass formula receive identical structural corrections when q_{\mathrm{eff}} replaces q_0.
